questions.q: Why is a written security policy considered a real security control, not just paperwork?
options: Because it's the agreed standard that technical controls are configured against, keeping enforcement consistent across the organization
Because policy documents are legally required to have no actual effect on systems
Because it replaces the need for any technical controls at all
Because only auditors ever read security policy documents
questions.explain: Without a written policy, different admins would configure controls based on their own guesses, and those standards would drift apart over time.

questions.q: What does an Acceptable Use Policy (AUP) primarily define?
options: What employees are and aren't allowed to do with company systems and data
The specific encryption algorithm used on all company laptops
The physical layout of the server room
Which cloud provider the company must use
questions.explain: The AUP sets the rules for employee behavior on company systems, such as not installing unauthorized software or using email for personal business.

questions.q: In the password policy example, what turns the written rule into an actual enforced control?
options: IT configuring the identity provider or Active Directory settings to require and check those rules automatically
Employees being asked nicely to follow the written rule
The rule being printed and posted on an office bulletin board
Nothing — the written policy enforces itself without any configuration
questions.explain: The written policy sentence becomes a real control only once the technical system is configured to require and enforce it for every user.

questions.q: What is the purpose of an incident response policy?
options: To define who gets notified, who has authority to act, and how evidence is handled when a breach occurs
To specify how often passwords must be changed
To list which software employees are allowed to install
To classify data as public or confidential
questions.explain: Having this decided ahead of time means the first hours of a real incident go toward containment instead of arguing about process.

questions.q: What does a data classification policy typically define?
options: Categories of data, such as public, confidential, or restricted, along with handling rules for each
The minimum password length required for all accounts
The escalation chain during a security incident
Which employees are allowed to use personal USB drives
questions.explain: Data classification tells employees how sensitive a piece of data is and what protection it requires, like whether it can be emailed externally.
